title: Pediatric Longitudinal Glomerular Disease: a PNRC Multi-Institutional Cohort Study
off: Pediatric Longitudinal Glomerular Disease: a PNRC Multi-Institutional Cohort Study
summary: To review and collect information from a patients medical record in order to study and research how to help other children with glomerular diseases.
desc:
This study is designed to look at the natural history of glomerular diseases in children and adolescents in order to direct the research to find cures. This study will also possibly help identify or locate participants that may be eligible for clinical trials.

Mixed retrospective-prospective cohort study (longitudinal, observational, non-interventional study) to research the natural history of glomerular disease in children and adolescents in the US.

Objective: Evaluate the natural history of glomerular disease in children in the United States.

Aim 1: To investigate and determine important relationships among patient/disease characteristics, natural history, treatments, histopathology, and outcomes among pediatric patients with glomerular disease, both across and within pre-specified disease cohorts (see below), by means of multicenter collection, storage, and analysis of longitudinal data.

Aim 2: To provide a platform for and facilitate, with participant consent, rapid assessment of potential participant eligibility for planned and/or ongoing investigator-initiated and/or industry-sponsored clinical trials of pediatric glomerular disease.

20 initial sites were selected to recruit participants with glomerular disease. Patients diagnosed starting in July 2023, as well as newly diagnosed patients can be enrolled. Participants will be followed until 21 years of age.

Data Collection at 6 month timepoints +/- 30 days. Collection starts with demographic information, medical history, and family medical history. Also collected at enrollment and at each time point are standard of care labs, hospitalizations, renal biopsy images, pathology reports and specialized or genetic testing. Participants will be asked to answer quality of life and social determinate of health questionnaires at enrollment and annually. These are optional and will not affect eligibility.

Enrollment expected to be 500 participants per year.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

Children with biopsy-proven glomerular disease or populations with a clinical diagnosis of glomerular disease

Exclusion Criteria:

Patients who declined (or unable to provide informed consent, + informed assent of minors) to participate Patients with End Stage Kidney Disease (Stage 5 CKD, eGFR \< 15mL/min/1.73m2)
